title: Decision Table
definition: A decision table enumerates relevant condition combinations and the action expected for each combination.
purpose: Expose missing, conflicting, and unreachable rules before implementation.
history: Decision tables have long been used in requirements analysis and systematic software testing to connect condition combinations with actions.
mental_model: Each column is one complete rule: given these condition values, perform exactly these stated actions.
analogy: A timetable maps a known situation to an action; the analogy fails when rules overlap, priority matters, or continuous ranges must first be partitioned.
industry_notes: A reviewed decision table can become a shared contract among product, engineering, and testing roles.
ai_notes: AI should not invent rule priorities; unclear or overlapping columns must be escalated as requirements questions.
interview_notes: Ask for a small table, completeness check, implementation order, and one infeasible case.
exercise_candidates: Build a shipping table from prose
lab_candidates: Implement and test every rule column
